PERHAPS THE REAL QUESTION SHOULD BE NOT WEATHER FUEL WAS TAXED HEAVILY BUT WHETHER THE RETURNS JUSTIFY THE BURDEN ON CONSUMERS. 
1. Let's look at Delhi. The buildup of petrol price in Delhi shows that there are four components - price charged to dealers by OMCs (cost + freight multiplied by exchange rate + margins if any), excise duty charged by central govt., dealer commission charged by petrol pump owners and VAT charged by state governments. In Jan 2014 (under UPA) price charged to dealers accounted for 67% of the total pump price, excise duty 13%, dealer commission 3% and VAT 17%. 
2. Now look at May 2026. You'll note that the build up of petrol prices (price charged to Dealers by OMC + Excise + pump owners commission + VAT) is strikingly same as UPA years. 

3. Let's look at where the monies realised from excise went. 
From May 2014 (under NDA) to July 2019, the NDA increased excise duty on petrol to keep the prices constant and did not pass on the benefit of crude oil price reduction to consumers, instead using these funds for funding welfare schemes and capex. 
4. As you can see from table below spend on CAPEX has increased 250% since UPA.

GOI has spent Rs. 65.5 lakh crore on capex in last 12 years and another Rs. 23.3 lakh crore on pet schemes of PM Modi like Ujjwala, Awas Yojana, Jal Jivan, Kisan Nidhi, Ayushman etc while continuing old schemes like NREGA and Gram Sadak Yojana. Together GOI has spent Rs. 88.8 lakh crore on these schemes and capex in the last 12 years.

8. This shows that the policy of GOI to collect excise duty improved state capacity and fiscal resources.

यह बात मैं हवा में नहीं कह रहा हूं। आज मैं खुद डीज़ल लेने गया था, लेकिन मुझे नहीं मिला। अगर आप डीज़ल दिलाने में मदद कर सकें तो बड़ी कृपा होगी। मुझे लगभग 50 बीघा खेत की जुताई करनी है, कृपया उसी हिसाब से डीज़ल उपलब्ध कराने की व्यवस्था करें।

The EIA just released new data on US oil inventories, exports/imports, & production, but one thing doesn’t make much sense at first glance…

Gasoline, diesel, and other distillate inventories are obviously declining as expected, but jet fuel inventories have held despite the global loss of medium grade crude, which usually generates the highest yield of jet fuel compared to other grades.

So how is this possible?

Looking at the full picture, CPP production in the US has increased across the board, but production of Jet fuel has increased much more compared to other refined products. And keep in mind this has happened while jet fuel imports decrease and exports increase.

What we’re likely looking at here is an overreaction of US refineries (especially ones owned by airlines) optimizing for kerosene based jet fuel production rather than gasoline. 

As a result jet fuel production has increased by nearly 300,000 bpd since the start of the war, while no meaningful decline is jet fuel consumption can be seen (yet).

As a result gasoline inventories have fallen nearly 50 million barrels (to a 10+ year low) while exports remain flat, imports from europe decrease, and production stalls comparatively.

For tankers, the result of this could result in lower gasoline exports due to tighter production and limited imports. While refineries could face more systematic stress for hydrocracker systems, potentially causing longer maintenance periods in the future.

If this continues there could be increasing pressure on US CPP exports due to these reasons which would  translate to lower clean tanker demand from the US, creating a negative impact on clean tanker rates. #tankers #oott
